article.title: Combine calendar apps on iPhone without losing track of events
article.short: Replace app switching with a checked overview
article.description: Bring calendar accounts into one iPhone overview. Check event destinations, duplicate routes, write-back and notifications before changing your daily workflow.
article.lede: A single calendar view can help you compare commitments across accounts. Start by checking what it includes and where changes are saved. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
article.commonBelief: Replacing several calendar apps means merging all calendars and deleting the old apps immediately.

sections.heading: Choose the job you need the overview to do
body: Write down the calendars that affect a real scheduling decision: your work meetings, personal appointments and a shared household schedule, for example. Identify their accounts and who owns each calendar. Several calendars under one Google account are still separate calendars.

Decide whether you need to see commitments together, edit their originals, or copy availability into another account. These are different jobs. A combined view helps you compare times; it does not by itself make colleagues see a personal appointment in their work scheduling system.

sections.heading: Check workplace approval before connecting
body: For a work account, use the connection method your organisation permits. Keep its approved app available when it is required for meeting responses, delegated access or other work tasks. A paid personal calendar app cannot grant missing permissions.

If a connection fails, record which account type and stage failed rather than repeatedly changing passwords or deleting accounts. An access decision, a connection error and a calendar that is merely hidden need different remedies. Ask your administrator when the permitted route is unclear.

sections.heading: Add accounts without assuming there are no copies
body: Cloud Calendars can present selected iOS calendars alongside connected Google and Microsoft calendars. Its provider connections use mirrored calendars in the iPhone calendar store. This is different from promising a display-only connection that never stores another representation of an event.

Before adding a second route to the same account, check how it already appears on the phone. A provider calendar available through iOS and through a separate app connection can be confusing to identify by name alone. Inspect the calendar and source instead of assuming similarly named entries are interchangeable.

sections.heading: Verify one disposable appointment in both directions
body: Create a harmless test appointment with a distinctive name in the intended writable calendar. Confirm it in the provider’s own view. Change its title there, return to the combined view and check the same record. Then make a small test change from the combined view and confirm it at the provider.

This checks your actual setup; it is not a guaranteed refresh-time test. Use an ordinary appointment you own, without guests or recurrence, so troubleshooting does not send changed invitations to other people. Keep real meetings unchanged until you understand which route is failing.

sections.heading: Narrow the view before deleting anything
body: If the overview has duplicates, temporarily hide one calendar and note which entry disappears. Compare account, calendar, organiser and time before deciding whether you have two stored records or two display routes. Repeated names are not enough evidence for deletion. Record the original selection and restore it after comparing. In Cloud Calendars, selection can also affect widgets, notification scheduling and Google synchronization.

Apple documents showing or hiding calendars using the calendar-list checkboxes. Hiding is a useful first display check; deleting a record or account can have wider effects. Preserve the source and any needed backup while you investigate.

sections.heading: Choose a routine after the checks pass
body: Keep the combined view as your usual planning screen if it covers the calendars you need. Keep another approved app for a task the overview does not support, such as a workplace-specific invitation workflow. Fewer switches can be useful without making one app responsible for every account function.

Check notifications separately. Seeing an event once does not establish that only one app or device will alert you. Cloud Calendars Base includes Google sync and calendar views; Advanced removes ads, while Premium adds Microsoft Calendar and Teams support. Check local prices and account permissions before subscribing.

practical: List the calendars and owning accounts needed for your planning overview.
Confirm workplace approval and keep any required work app.
Check existing account routes before adding another provider connection.
Trace one disposable appointment to the provider and back.
Hide a suspected duplicate calendar before considering deletion.
Review alerts independently of the visible calendar view.

faq.q: Must I delete the other calendar apps?
faq.a: No. Keep required apps and preserve your current setup while checking the new overview. Use each app for the tasks you have verified.

faq.q: Will my colleagues see that my personal time is busy?
faq.a: A combined view on your phone does not establish that another account receives availability. That is a separate sharing or synchronization requirement.

faq.q: Does connecting a provider mean data stays only at the provider?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Cloud Calendars uses mirrored provider calendars in the iOS calendar store. Check the actual account route and storage context before connecting sensitive calendars.

article.title: Work and personal calendars in one app: keep ownership separate
article.description: See work and personal calendars together without merging ownership. Check permissions, event destinations and Cloud Calendars plans before connecting accounts.
article.lede: An overview can help you spot clashes while keeping event ownership clear. Check both the calendars you display and the account routes used to store their copies. This guide is written by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
article.commonBelief: Putting work and personal calendars in one app also combines their sharing permissions.

sections.heading: An overview is different from shared access
body: A calendar app can display selected calendars together while each keeps its own account and permissions. Apple’s multiple-calendar guide describes choosing calendars to display, assigning colours and selecting a default calendar. Those display choices are not a transfer of event ownership.

Before connecting a work account, check your organisation’s requirements. Google documents that administrators can restrict calendar sharing. A convenient personal overview does not give you permission to publish work details or bypass account restrictions.

Cloud Calendars’ Google and Microsoft connections use mirrored calendars in the iPhone calendar store. The available calendar sources can affect where these copies are held. A work-account connection therefore needs approval for its actual data flow, not just for the account name shown in the overview.

sections.heading: Use colour and visibility for the overview
body: Give work and personal calendars distinct colours, then check a busy day with both visible. When you want a narrower view, hide a calendar rather than deleting its events. Apple’s duplicate-calendar guide explains how to show and hide calendars with checkboxes. Before accepting a new commitment, restore the calendars relevant to that decision and compare the week with all of them visible. An empty filtered view does not establish that the time is free.

Hiding a calendar does not change who has permission to access it. In Cloud Calendars, calendar selection also matters to Google synchronization and notification scheduling, so do not assume that deselecting a calendar affects only the picture on screen. Check important changes at their provider and review notification settings separately if the goal is a quiet evening. Keep an approved work app available if your organisation requires it.

sections.heading: Check the destination before saving
body: A default calendar is a useful starting point, not a guarantee that every appointment belongs there. For a personal appointment, check the selected calendar before saving. For a work meeting, use the work calendar and the organisation’s invitation process.

Do not move or copy an invitation simply to make it appear in your overview. Microsoft distinguishes events you created from meetings organised by someone else: changing your own displayed copy is not a reliable way to update the organiser or attendees. Keep the original invitation and ask the organiser about a time change.

sections.heading: What the Cloud Calendars plans add
body: Cloud Calendars supports calendar views on iPhone and iPad. Its Base plan includes Google Calendar sync and the multi-calendar view. Advanced adds ad removal; Premium adds Microsoft Calendar and Teams support. Current local prices are shown in the app and App Store.

Advanced is not a paid permission to manage every account. A subscription does not make a read-only calendar writable or override workplace policy. Local calendars can be used without an account; provider connections and sharing have their own sign-in requirements.

sections.heading: Check a privacy-preserving busy block from the other side
body: Suppose a personal appointment should stop colleagues booking that time, but they should not learn its title. Seeing it beside work on your phone is only your overview. First establish whether your work account contains any availability entry at all, then check what an intended colleague can see.

If your organisation permits a manual work availability block, review the destination, title, notes, location, attendees and availability before saving. Avoid copying private appointment details into it. This is an approved arrangement you create and verify, not an automatic Cloud Calendars masking feature. Keep later changes consistent without turning the second entry into another invitation.

practical: Check whether your workplace permits the account connection.
Choose distinct colours and display the calendars you need for an overview.
Verify the destination calendar when creating a new event.
Hide a calendar temporarily to narrow the view; do not delete events to tidy it.
Review sharing permissions and notifications separately from calendar visibility.

faq.q: Will my employer see my personal events just because both calendars are in one app?
faq.a: Displaying calendars together does not itself grant calendar-sharing permission. Check which account owns each event, its sharing settings and any employer device-management rules. Do not save a private appointment to a work calendar by accident.

faq.q: Do I need Advanced to see Google and personal calendars together?
faq.a: Google Calendar sync and the multi-calendar view are Base features. Advanced removes ads. Microsoft Calendar support is part of Premium; account permissions still apply.

faq.q: Does Cloud Calendars automatically replace personal details with a work busy block?
faq.a: Do not rely on that. Viewing calendars together and creating provider mirrors are different from an explicit privacy-masking rule that copies availability into another account. Verify the arrangement your organisation permits.

article.title: Week calendar on iPhone: compare hours without overlooking commitments
article.description: Read a week calendar on iPhone: check the first day, week numbers, date range and selected calendars before offering an apparent gap.
article.lede: A week grid helps compare when commitments begin and end. Start with the dates and calendars it represents, then use the details when a small block or shortened title leaves a question unanswered. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
article.commonBelief: Every visible gap is available time, and every commitment appears as a timed block.

sections.heading: Check which week and calendars you are reading
body: Read the date range and day labels before placing an appointment. A selected range is not necessarily the week you had in mind. Check that the work, family or other calendars relevant to this decision are selected, rather than assuming every connected calendar is currently visible.

For example, a personal view may hide a work calendar to reduce clutter. The clear afternoon it shows does not establish that the work schedule is empty. Bring the relevant calendars into view before offering the slot, and confirm the account behind an unfamiliar colour.

sections.heading: Separate the first weekday from other date-display settings
body: If two calendar views begin on different days, compare their date headers before changing an appointment. A fixed week beginning on Monday or Sunday is different from a rolling view beginning today or on a selected date. Check the settings offered by the app and version you are using, then reopen the view to verify its actual range. Do not move events merely to make two grids look alike.

Apple documents these choices in Settings > Apps > Calendar: Start Week On chooses a weekday, while Week View Starts On Today changes the week-view starting point. Fantastical likewise separates Start Week On from Start Week View On. These are instructions for those applications; changing an Apple Calendar display preference does not establish that every other calendar app will adopt it.

Week numbers are another setting. Apple documents Week Numbers, and Fantastical documents Show Calendar Weeks with an optional custom starting date. If a colleague asks for “week 12,” confirm the year and actual start and end dates, especially when comparing different systems or a range near New Year. Choosing Monday as the first column does not by itself establish which week-numbering convention is in use.

Alternate date labels are also different from calendar accounts. Apple’s Alternate Calendars setting can show Chinese, Hebrew or Hijri dates alongside Gregorian dates. That display choice is not a connection to another person’s calendar or an import of a holiday schedule. Read the actual event date before agreeing a booking, and do not assume another app offers the same dual-date display.

For a shared plan, write the date range explicitly rather than relying only on a week number or the first column in a screenshot. Check the selected calendars again before offering time. If your installed app lacks a display option you need, consult the relevant provider view and compare the dates; do not treat an unfamiliar label as evidence that the underlying event must be rescheduled.

sections.heading: Use blocks to compare time, then open the details
body: Compare start, end and overlap on the hour grid. A narrow event can be hard to read, so open it to check the full title, location and calendar. Do not infer a precise duration from the apparent size of a small block alone.

If two appointments overlap, first establish whether they are separate commitments or two displays of the same record. Similar titles and matching times do not prove duplication. Temporarily hide one calendar to identify the source instead of deleting an invitation to clear the grid.

sections.heading: Read all-day events separately from the hourly gaps
body: Cloud Calendars separates all-day events from timed events in its multi-day display. Inspect that area as well as the hour columns. A holiday, trip or all-day commitment can matter even when the timed grid looks empty.

An all-day label does not by itself tell you which hours you can offer to someone else. Open the event and understand its actual meaning. For travel over several days, check the start and end dates rather than assuming a single visible label describes every affected day.

sections.heading: Include the parts of the plan that are not yet appointments
body: A calendar can only display the information available to it. A journey, preparation or recovery period may need its own agreed block if it affects a booking. Seeing space between two saved meetings does not establish that you can travel between their locations in that interval.

For a workshop after an existing appointment, write down the real travel and setup requirements before choosing a start. This is a planning method, not a claim that Cloud Calendars automatically calculates travel buffers or reserves time in colleagues’ scheduling systems.

For a confirmed shift from Monday at 22:00 to Tuesday at 06:00, record a timed event with Tuesday explicitly set as the ending date. Reopen the saved event to check both dates, times, calendar and relevant time zone. A Monday label alone does not communicate the Tuesday finish. Before offering a Tuesday morning appointment, allow for your actual journey home and recovery needs. Use the employer’s confirmed rota for the shift itself. If it repeats, follow the recurrence guide below and use a rule only when it matches that rota; a personal calendar change does not approve a shift swap.

sections.heading: Switch to a closer view before a consequential edit
body: If the selected range needs more space than the viewport, Cloud Calendars can scroll the day columns rather than squeeze them all into view. Check the day labels as you scroll. Open the day or the event details when a particular commitment needs closer inspection.

Before dragging or resizing an event, check its calendar, intended local time and repeat scope. After saving a permitted change, reopen it and verify the result. A successful-looking gesture does not prove that the owning service and every participant have accepted the new arrangement.

sections.heading: Keep view controls and weather coverage in context
body: Apple Calendar and Teamup document their own week-view controls. Teamup also distinguishes browser configuration from mobile views. Those instructions do not establish the same controls inside Cloud Calendars; choose the view from the app you are actually using.

A week of appointments is not a guarantee of complete weather information for every day or place. For an outdoor slot, check the selected forecast location and available date and hours separately. Then communicate the final arrangement through the agreed channel.

practical: Check the date range and selected calendars.
Compare the actual date range, first weekday and any week-number or alternate-date labels before relying on a screenshot or a numbered work week.
Read exact start and end times when a block is unclear.
Inspect all-day commitments as well as timed events.
Account for real travel and preparation before offering a gap.
Confirm editing permission, local time and recurrence scope.
Reopen the saved event and confirm important changes directly.

faq.q: Does a blank part of the week mean everyone is free?
faq.a: No. It reflects the calendars and information currently displayed. Check hidden commitments and confirm availability with the people involved.

faq.q: Why can a week look empty despite an all-day commitment?
faq.a: All-day events are displayed separately from timed blocks. Inspect that area and open the event before offering the time.

faq.q: Should I drag an event whose title I cannot read?
faq.a: Open its details first. Confirm its identity, calendar, time and intended edit scope before changing it.

faq.q: Does starting the week on Monday also set the week numbers?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The first weekday, rolling-view alignment and week-number labels are separate choices in the documented Apple and Fantastical workflows. Confirm the displayed dates and the convention used by the person sharing the plan.

article.title: A weekly calendar review: commitments, time blocks and shared responsibilities
article.short: Review the week before adding more
article.description: A practical weekly calendar review: check selected calendars, fixed commitments, travel and shared responsibilities before saving realistic time blocks.
article.lede: Use a short review to identify what is already fixed and what still needs a decision. The routine below is a suggested workflow, not a promise that every week can be organised in ten minutes. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
article.commonBelief: Adding enough time blocks automatically makes a realistic plan and tells everyone what they are responsible for.

sections.heading: Start with the right dates and calendars
body: Open the intended week and select the calendars relevant to the plan. Read the date range, not just the weekday labels. A personal view with work hidden can make an unavailable afternoon look clear; a combined view does not automatically share those commitments with anyone else.

Choose one ordinary appointment from each important calendar and check that it appears on the expected date. If a source is missing or stale, resolve that comparison before building the week around an apparent gap. Do not remove an account or duplicate a meeting just to make the overview look complete.

sections.heading: Separate fixed commitments from proposed blocks
body: Keep an agreed lesson, client appointment or booked journey at its real time. A block for writing, preparation or errands is a proposal you control; it is not the same as an invitation someone else has accepted. Label a provisional block clearly when another decision is still needed.

For example, a report due on Friday may need preparation earlier in the week. Estimate the work from the actual task and choose a block that fits around existing commitments. There is no universal rule that exactly three discretionary items will fit everyone’s week.

If Tuesday’s 45-minute preparation block ends with half a report still to write, estimate the remaining work and choose another realistic opening around agreed appointments. Keep Friday’s 17:00 deadline separate: moving the preparation block does not move the deadline. A calendar block records planned time, so check the task itself before calling it finished.

sections.heading: Include the transitions that use the gaps
body: Check location and actual start and end times. Travel, setup and a handoff can consume a gap between two appointments even when the hour grid shows empty space. Use a suitable route estimate for the intended time, and keep uncertainty or venue requirements in the plan.

For an afternoon workshop, distinguish the public start from arrival and preparation. If separate entries help, label them so a helper does not confuse a departure block with the workshop itself. This planning convention is not a claim that a personal block automatically reserves time in every connected provider’s availability system.

sections.heading: Agree responsibilities, not just attendance
body: A family activity on the calendar may still lack a person responsible for collection. Agree who will act, when and where; record the decision in the intended shared calendar and obtain a direct confirmation. A name in an event title is not an automatic assignment.

Choose the audience deliberately. A private work calendar is not a family handoff channel, and a widely shared schedule may not be suitable for sensitive notes. Check the actual destination and permissions before relying on the entry being visible to someone else.

sections.heading: Check weather-dependent plans against available information
body: For an outdoor commitment, inspect the forecast’s selected place, date and hours. An appointment can exist beyond the available forecast range. A blank value is unavailable information, not evidence of dry weather, and a lower rain probability does not by itself describe rain amount or duration.

Choose an appropriate alternative with the people or venue involved and record when the decision will be confirmed. Do not promise that selecting a different hour will avoid a shower or that saving a fallback makes the app relocate the event automatically.

sections.heading: Save the right destination and review the result
body: Before saving a new block, check its calendar, date, time zone, duration and any alert. For a repeating commitment, read the intended edit scope instead of rewriting a series to represent one exception. Apple’s multiple-calendar guide describes destination changes in Apple Calendar; use the controls in the app and provider you are actually using.

Reopen the entries you changed, check an important later occurrence and confirm shared changes through the agreed channel. End the review with a short list of unresolved decisions and who will confirm them. A tidy calendar is a useful reference, not proof that the work, travel or handoff has happened.

practical: Confirm the week and selected calendars.
Identify agreed commitments and label provisional blocks.
Include real travel, setup and handoff requirements.
Agree the responsible person and confirm shared access.
Check available weather information and an appropriate alternative.
Verify saved destinations, alerts and repeat scope, then confirm changes.

faq.q: Must the review take exactly ten minutes?
faq.a: No. Use a short review as a starting habit. The needed time depends on missing information and the decisions involved.

faq.q: Does a time block reserve my availability everywhere?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Check the owning provider and the calendars used for scheduling; a personal combined view is not automatic availability copying.

faq.q: Does adding someone’s name assign the task?
faq.a: No. This workflow records an agreement. Confirm the responsibility and the person’s access separately.

article.title: Calendar notifications on iPhone: missing, silent or duplicated?
article.description: Separate event alerts, Cloud Calendars settings and iPhone delivery controls. Diagnose absent, silent or duplicate reminders without deleting calendar data.
article.lede: Start with what actually happened: was the event missing, was its notification absent, did it appear without sound, or did two apps alert you? Each points to a different check. This guide is published by Arte Soft, the developer of Cloud Calendars.
article.commonBelief: If an event appears in the calendar, every alert and notification permission must already be configured.

sections.heading: First choose the right branch
body: If the event itself is absent, check its owning account and selected calendar before changing sound settings. An alert cannot establish whether the correct event has reached the app. Use the calendar-sync guide for that separate problem.

If the event is visible but no notification appears, check the saved alert and both notification controls below. If a notification appears silently, concentrate on iPhone delivery and sound settings. If you receive more than one, identify each sending app and each configured alert before removing anything.

sections.heading: No notification: inspect the event and app controls
body: Open the event and inspect its alert time. The Cloud Calendars event editor has Alert and, when applicable, Second Alert controls, including None and choices before the event. A second alert can be intentional. Check the saved event again after an edit, especially when a provider or shared-calendar permission limits what you can change.

In Cloud Calendars settings, look for Event Notifications. The settings also separate invitation and weather notifications; enabling one is not proof that ordinary event reminders are enabled. Check both the app’s Event Notifications preference and iOS notification permission.

Calendar selection also matters: the current scheduling path uses alarms from selected calendars. Check that the relevant calendar is selected. Do not assume hiding a calendar changes only its appearance in this app, and do not delete events to stop reminders.

sections.heading: A silent or delayed alert: check iPhone delivery
body: In the iPhone Settings app, open Notifications and choose Cloud Calendars. Review Allow Notifications, the available alert locations and sound controls. Check whether Scheduled Summary or an active Focus is changing delivery. These are Apple’s system settings, not the Alert menu inside an event. Labels can vary with iOS version.

A banner seen without sound is a different observation from no notification anywhere. Note whether it appeared on the Lock Screen or in Notification Center, whether the phone was in use, and which Focus was active. Change one relevant setting at a time so the next result tells you something. A Live Activity countdown is another surface; seeing it does not prove an audible reminder will arrive.

sections.heading: Two alerts: identify the senders before changing the event
body: Read the app name on each notification. Apple Calendar, Google Calendar and Cloud Calendars can be separate notification sources even when they display related events. Two notifications are not enough evidence that two event records exist. Also compare the alert times: a reminder the day before and another near the start may match the saved alert choices.

Google’s notification guide explains that its settings are personal to the account and that event-specific choices can differ from calendar defaults. Its instructions apply to Google Calendar, not to Cloud Calendars settings. Inspect the relevant sender rather than assuming one app’s switch controls every other app.

Choose which app you want to notify you, then adjust only the relevant reminder or notification preference. If two actual event records remain, compare their calendars and ownership using the duplicate-event guide. Do not cancel a real meeting just to silence an extra alert.

sections.heading: Use one disposable event to narrow the problem
body: Create a clearly named test appointment in a writable calendar you own. Set its start far enough ahead that the chosen alert time is still in the future. Confirm the calendar is selected, the saved alert is present, and both notification controls are enabled. Record the expected alert time and which app should send it.

Observe whether a notification appears and whether it makes sound; those are separate results. Repeat only after changing one suspected setting. Use an ordinary test event without attendees, not an important meeting or a recurring series. Keep the result with your app and iOS versions so you can compare later.

sections.heading: If the result is still inconsistent
body: The app schedules a limited set of upcoming alarms; do not rely on an unlimited queue of distant reminders. Check the controls in your installed version and keep a record of inconsistent delivery. Report the app and iOS versions, calendar type, saved alert offset, expected time and observed result.

Keep private event titles, attendee addresses and calendar subscription links out of a public report. Reinstalling, clearing local storage or removing accounts is not the first diagnostic step. Preserve the event and account arrangement while support investigates.

practical: Classify the failure: missing event, absent notification, silent delivery or duplicate alerts.
Check the saved alert and selected calendar.
Check Cloud Calendars Event Notifications separately from iPhone notification permission.
For duplicates, compare sending apps and configured alert times.
Use one disposable future event and record the result without changing real invitations.

faq.q: Does turning on weather notifications enable event reminders?
faq.a: No. The app settings separate event, invitation and weather notifications. Check Event Notifications and iOS permission for ordinary event alarms.

faq.q: Should I delete one event when two alerts arrive?
faq.a: First identify the sending apps and alert times. Multiple notifications can come from separate apps or multiple alerts on one event. Deletion is not a safe way to diagnose that.

faq.q: Does an alert setting guarantee delivery?
faq.a: No. It is one part of the chain. App preferences, system permission and delivery settings also matter, so check the result on your device.
